newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Commission suspends meeting on Di Rupo.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Commission suspends meeting on Di Rupo.

text.p: A special Belgian parliamentary commission said on Tuesday it was suspending a meeting to assess fresh allegations of child sex against Deputy Prime Minister Elio Di Rupo.

Raymond Langendries, the president of parliament who also chairs the commission, told reporters the panel would hear the prosecutor general of the country's highest court and also Di Rupo himself later on Tuesday.

Eliane Lieckendael, the prosecutor general of the Cour de Cassation -- the only Belgian court which can try ministers and ex-ministers -- was due to appear before the commission, made up of the main parties, at 10:30 a.m. (0930 GMT).
Di Rupo was due to appear at 2:00 p.m.

One of the commission's members, Pierre Chevalier of the Flemish liberal VLD party, said the dossier under review was more substantial than an initial set of allegations made by a sole witness, whom the court had termed unreliable.
"In any case I think this is somewhat more substantial than has been the case so far," he said after the meeting, which had begun at around 6:00 p.m. on Monday.
